identityTradability.exchangeName: Comfort Systems USA, Inc. Common Stock

thesisQuality.basis: Strong demand, backlog, cash conversion and margin expansion support durable adoption/value capture, but concentration and contractor substitutability keep the assessment below exceptional.

financialOperatingMomentum.basis: Revenue, EPS, gross margin, operating cash flow and backlog all accelerated materially in Q2/H1 2026 with strong funding capacity.

marketValuationOpportunity.basis: Operating growth is exceptional, but approximately 40.19x trailing earnings and $57.46B market capitalization embed demanding expectations and limit valuation headroom.

catalystScore.basis: Record backlog, strong pipelines and continued 2026-2027 demand visibility provide material identifiable operating catalysts, though backlog timing is not guaranteed.

governancePower.basis: Current filings show strong execution and cash conversion with no present accounting blocker; decentralized project execution and cost-to-cost accounting warrant ongoing control monitoring.

alignment2036.basis: Electrical, mechanical and modular execution is directly exposed to critical data-center power/cooling and broader industrial infrastructure buildout.

crossDivisionLeverage.basis: Core mechanical/electrical/modular capabilities serve technology, industrial and institutional markets across multiple U.S. operations, but current growth is meaningfully technology-led.

bottleneckControl.basis: Scaled skilled electrical/mechanical/modular execution participates in a real deployment constraint, but the company does not control an irreplaceable proprietary bottleneck.

scenarioRobustness.basis: Diversified contracting capabilities and service markets support multiple demand scenarios, offset by meaningful exposure to the current hyperscale/data-center build cycle.

substitutionResilience.basis: Scale, reputation, workforce and execution capability create replacement friction, but competing contractors, owner self-performance and alternative modular suppliers remain credible substitutes.

supplyChainResilience.basis: Execution scale and operating breadth provide some resilience, while filings identify labor, subcontractor and supplier capacity as material constraints without evidence sufficient for an 80-band multi-source conclusion.

pricingPower.basis: Gross margin expansion to 25.9% alongside rapid revenue growth and backlog supports strong economic capture, while project-based contracting prevents an exceptional structural-pricing conclusion.

riskEvidence.basis: Primary risks are premium valuation, technology/data-center concentration, backlog conversion, fixed-price estimating, labor and supplier constraints; strong cash generation and backlog temper but do not remove them.

dataConfidenceEvidence.basis: Identity/tradability and operating claims are supported by SEC/issuer primary evidence and current valuation by an independent market source; customer concentration remains incompletely quantified.

scoreRecord.thesis: Comfort Systems is a scaled execution beneficiary of power/cooling/electrical infrastructure demand, with record backlog, cash generation and margin expansion supporting a strong operating thesis, while premium valuation and project/data-center concentration constrain asymmetry.
scoreRecord.keyRisk: A slowdown in hyperscale/data-center construction or execution pressure in labor, suppliers and fixed-price projects could compress growth and margins while the premium valuation amplifies downside.
scoreRecord.nextCatalyst: Q3 2026 earnings and backlog update, currently expected in October 2026, to test continued backlog conversion, margins and technology-demand durability.
